label: GitHub
terms_note: Acceptable Use Policies forbid spam and bulk unsolicited activity. The binding cap is the secondary limit: 80 content-generating requests per minute and 500 per hour (5,000 requests/hour primary).

auth: 1. Fine-grained personal access token (repo-scoped: Contents, Discussions, Issues write) or a GitHub App installation
2. `gh` CLI (`gh auth login`) covers the same surface for scripts; the official MCP server exposes it to agents.

endpoints.call: REST `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases` {tag_name, name, body, draft, prerelease} + upload assets

reference.limits: - Primary: 5,000 requests/hour per user token (15,000 Enterprise Cloud; installations ≥ 5,000 scaling to 12,500), 60/hour unauthenticated; GraphQL 5,000 points/hour. - Secondary: ≤ 100 concurrent requests, 900 REST points/minute, **≤ 80 content-generating requests per minute and 500 per hour** (the binding cap for a posting agent); headers `x-ratelimit-*`, 403/429 with `retry-after`. - GitHub Acceptable Use Policies: no spam, no bulk unsolicited activity; content is public and indexed (links in READMEs are nofollow; Discussions / Releases still drive exposure).

fields.name: token
fields.help: GitHub personal access token (fine-grained: repository permission Discussions read / write on the repositories used; classic: repo or public_repo scope) sent as 'Authorization: bearer TOKEN' (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/forming-calls-with-graphql).

adapter.envelope_note: GraphQL answers HTTP 200 with {data: null, errors: [...]} when a query fails as a whole (bad node id type, missing permission); such a body is an error result carrying the errors array as its message. REST GET /user has no data member and is unaffected.
adapter.terms: GraphQL: 5,000 points per hour per user; mutations cost at least 5 points and secondary rate limits apply to content creation (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/rate-limits-and-query-limits-for-the-graphql-api).

me.note: GET /user returns the token's user {login, id, node_id, name, html_url, ...}.

body.query: =query($id: ID!, $first: Int!) { node(id: $id) { ... on Discussion { comments(first: $first) { totalCount nodes { id body createdAt url author { login } } } } } }

read_comments.note: Top-level comments of a discussion: `post_id` is the discussion's GraphQL node id (e.g. D_kwDO...; the `id` field of a Discussion, not its number). Discussion.comments is cursor-paginated (first / after): only the first `limit` (max 100) comments are returned and `page` is not honoured; replies to comments are not included. A node id that is not a Discussion yields an empty list.

delete.note: DESTRUCTIVE: the deleteDiscussion mutation permanently deletes the discussion with node id `post_id` and all its comments (needs maintain / admin on the repository or authorship). Failures come back as a GraphQL errors array.

body.query: =query($id: ID!) { node(id: $id) { ... on Discussion { id url title comments { totalCount } reactions { totalCount } } } }

analytics_post.note: Counts for one discussion (node id): comments.totalCount and reactions.totalCount as top-level fields; there are no view counts in the API.

not_offered.publish_text: createDiscussion requires a title as well as a body, plus repositoryId and categoryId ('title: String! The title of the new discussion', https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/using-the-graphql-api-for-discussions#creatediscussion); the vocabulary input carries only text, and splitting a title out of it would be a guess.
not_offered.publish_image: Discussions take Markdown bodies only; there is no image upload in the GraphQL API (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/using-the-graphql-api-for-discussions#creatediscussion).
not_offered.reply_comment: addDiscussionComment requires the discussion's node id (discussionId: ID!) besides replyToId (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/using-the-graphql-api-for-discussions#adddiscussioncomment); a comment id alone cannot address it.
not_offered.read_mentions: The GraphQL Discussions API has no mentions feed; mentions surface as notifications (REST GET /notifications) that mix every reason and cannot be filtered to mentions server-side (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/activity/notifications).

evidence: host api.github.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Sectigo Limited)
probe: 4/4 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific

spec https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/rest-api-description/main/descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json, https://docs.github.com/public/fpt/schema.docs.graphql: 4/4 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
